adjacent.bodyExcerpt:
Recover RE-012 / transport's conditional prepared-write progress kernel on
node115. The active tree had no Rust implementation of this transition. The
new dependency-free no_std library separates the initial wrapping counter
charge from per-helper progress: partial writes advance pointer/remaining,
zero progress on nonempty input selects the native error-transform operand,
pending preserves the prepared slice, and oversized results expose the
pre-panic sentinel stores. A zero remaining count bypasses the helper.

adjacent.head: a4efaa5e293379f8974c434531785d95dee1dff4
adjacent.bodyExcerpt:
RE-001: what the node #115 lu.rs conversion's passed-through context pointer
points to, and what the coop-path call does with it.

Packet #184 (PR #2125) left open what the conversion's context pointer points
to and what the 0x5cf3b90 coop-path call does with it. Answer: the context
pointer P points to a pointer Q, and Q is a (function table, payload) pair.
The coop callee either tail-calls the table's slot 2 with the payload, or
hands (cell+0x20, Q) to a dedup-caching proceed function that calls the
table's slot 0 with the payload unless the last cached pair already equals
(Q[0], Q[1]). The choice is driven by a Tokio thread-local coop budget cell.

adjacent.title: RE-001: node #115 lu.rs tag 1 vs 3 is empty-vs-set state, not equality — the 0x5cf2d30 helper is Tokio time code
adjacent.head: 90dfec6a4f1202830fad93a8cddba3e75a67ba44
adjacent.bodyExcerpt:
RE-001: answer #183's open question — what decides lu.rs tag 1 vs 3.

Packet #183 (PR #2106, open) mapped the node #115 lu.rs f64 conversion and
left open whether its callee at 0x5cf2d30 decides tag 1 vs 3 by
value-equality or by identity. Answer: neither. The helper performs no
comparison of two values and no comparison of two pointers. It returns false
exactly when the output struct is in the empty/reset state, true otherwise —
so tag 1 = empty state, tag 3 = set state.

Resolve RE-012 / transport's selected deadline operand on one measured node115 greeting call. The caller stores zero beside binary64 60.0; the sender tests the first word's low byte and selects binary64 20.0 for that setup. The packet binds initial and resume copies, the chunk-local selector, and the selected word's route through a separately authenticated conversion body into pair addition. Clock/source type identities and actual deadline firing remain unclosed, so this is a conditional static constraint for reconstruction.
